content.text: Ethacrynic acid isn't in this vocabulary. Now let me run the full analysis using the three loop-diuretic ingredients (furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide), defining new users by first-ever drug exposure and checking for serum/plasma potassium < 3.5 mmol/L within 30 days.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH loop_drugs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS drug_concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (956874, 932745, 942350)
),
first_exposure AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS index_date
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN loop_drugs ld ON de.drug_concept_id = ld.drug_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id
),
potassium_meas AS (
  SELECT fe.person_id
  FROM first_exposure fe
  JOIN omop.measurement m
    ON m.person_id = fe.person_id
   AND m.measurement_concept_id = 3023103
   AND m.value_as_number < 3.5
   AND m.measurement_date >= fe.index_date
   AND m.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day, 30, fe.index_date)
  GROUP BY fe.person_id
)
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM first_exposure) AS n_new_users,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM potassium_meas) AS n_hypokalemia,
  CAST( (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM potassium_meas) AS FLOAT)
    / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM first_exposure),0) * 100 AS pct_hypokalemia

content.text:
**~23.6% of new loop-diuretic users had a serum/plasma potassium < 3.5 mmol/L within 30 days.**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| New loop-diuretic users | 102,203 |
| With hypokalemia (K⁺ < 3.5) within 30 days | 24,072 |
| Proportion | **23.55%** |

**Definitions used:**
- **New user** = first-ever `drug_exposure` to a loop diuretic (furosemide, bumetanide, or torsemide — including all RxNorm descendants; ethacrynic acid not present in this vocabulary). Index date = earliest exposure.
- **Hypokalemia** = at least one serum/plasma potassium (LOINC concept 3023103, *Potassium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma*) with `value_as_number < 3.5` on/within 30 days of the index date.

**Caveats:** This is a proportion among all new users, not restricted to those who actually had a potassium drawn in the window — so it understates the rate *among those tested*. It also doesn't require prior enrollment/washout (a true incident-user design would require a lookback period with no diuretic), and mmol/L vs mEq/L are numerically equivalent for potassium so the unit isn't filtered.
